Confusable pairs among alcohol and drug rules, followed by continuation facts the C block left out for size; each block ties to one handbook page, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec10-R01 | anchor: A02
The adult limit is a BAC of 0.08 percent, while a driver under 21 breaks the law at just 0.01 percent. [A02]
Why it matters: group BAC limits; confusable adult versus underage limit.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0117]

FACT_ID: sec10-R02 | anchor: A02
Crash risk roughly doubles just above 0.05 percent BAC, climbs to six times at 0.10 percent and to 25 times at 0.15 percent. [A02]
Why it matters: group BAC risk; confusable the three risk multiples.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0117]

FACT_ID: sec10-R03 | anchor: A02
Eating slows alcohol absorption, but heavy drinking always produces a high BAC whatever was eaten. [A02]
Why it matters: group BAC factors; misconception food prevents intoxication.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0117]

FACT_ID: sec10-R04 | anchor: A03
Slow driving can also signal impairment, because an intoxicated driver may be overly cautious and fall below the normal flow of traffic. [A03]
Why it matters: group impaired-driver signs; misconception only fast drivers are drunk.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0118]

FACT_ID: sec10-R05 | anchor: A03
Weaving can show up even when an intoxicated driver stays inside the correct lane, because holding a straight line becomes hard. [A03]
Why it matters: group impaired-driver signs; difficulty medium.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0118]

FACT_ID: sec10-R06 | anchor: A03
Jerky driving means short mental lapses that keep an intoxicated driver from holding a steady speed on a clear road, and quick stops mean braking suddenly at a sign or light instead of easing up. [A03]
Why it matters: group impaired-driver signs; confusable jerking motion versus quick stops.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0118]

FACT_ID: sec10-R07 | anchor: A02
The surest way to avoid a drinking-and-driving crash is not to drive at all after drinking, and the manual suggests a designated driver, public transportation or a cab instead. [A02]
Why it matters: group prevention; difficulty low.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0117]

FACT_ID: sec10-R08 | anchor: A01
Alcohol paired with anger accounts for much of the reckless, aggressive driving behind fatal highway crashes. [A01]
Why it matters: group alcohol effects; difficulty medium.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0116]

FACT_ID: sec10-R09 | anchor: A04
A designated driver takes responsibility for getting friends or family who have been drinking home safely, which also protects other motorists. [A04]
Why it matters: group prevention; difficulty low.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0119]

FACT_ID: sec10-R10 | anchor: A04
Never combine drugs without asking a medical professional about side effects and driving, and never mix alcohol with any drug or medication. [A04]
Why it matters: group drugs; difficulty low.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0119]

FACT_ID: sec10-R11 | anchor: A04
Ask a professional how an over-the-counter drug may affect driving, because legal medicines can still impair. [A04]
Why it matters: group drugs; misconception legal means safe to drive.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0119]

FACT_ID: sec10-R12 | anchor: A05
Any health problem, even a stiff neck, a cough or a sore leg, can interfere with driving, so let someone else drive when you feel unwell. [A05]
Why it matters: group health; difficulty low.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0120]

FACT_ID: sec10-R13 | anchor: A05
Good side (peripheral) vision lets a driver notice things out of the corners of the eyes while still looking straight ahead. [A05]
Why it matters: group vision; difficulty medium.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0120]

FACT_ID: sec10-R14 | anchor: A05
Poor distance judgment is a frequent cause of crashes, so a driver should always know how far the vehicle is from nearby objects. [A05]
Why it matters: group vision; difficulty low.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0120]

FACT_ID: sec10-R15 | anchor: A05
Hearing matters because horns, sirens and screeching tires give warnings, so keep the radio low and never drive wearing earphones. [A05]
Why it matters: group hearing; difficulty low.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0120]

FACT_ID: sec10-R16 | anchor: A05
State law allows the MVC to retest the driving population. [A05]
Why it matters: group vision; difficulty medium.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0120]
